Subject: APAC/US/EU node estimates for Helix deal — country split & fallback ask

Hi team,

Helix just moved to LOI and they're asking for a tri-region dedicated footprint with predictable latency for their core assist endpoint. Initial asks are: country-level traffic split, a recommended steady-state node count per region, and an emergency fallback plan if we hit supply constraints.

Quick context:
- Expected steady QPS: 38k globally (see attached estimates)
- Peak concurrency target: 900 concurrent requests across the fleet
- Models: mix of 13B and 70B (primarily quantized L4 paths)
- SLO: 95th percentile tail <= 220ms token latency for 13B, <= 420ms for 70B

What I need from this thread by EOD Thursday (26 Aug):
1) Per-region steady-state node counts (US / EU / APAC) + headroom percentage for burst
2) Canary rollout order and fallback lane if APAC capacity is constrained
3) Preliminary cost delta between immediate provision vs tranche-based commit

Attachments: helix_moa_traffic_estimates.xlsx (traffic by country), tri-region-fallback-sketch.pdf

Thanks — I'm looping in procurement (procurement@helix.ai) and ops (ops@helix.ai) so they see the ask. Rishi/karthik — can you own the sizing? Laura/Ben — can you put together cost / SOW outline?

—Monica

Subject: Re: APAC/US/EU node estimates for Helix deal — country split & fallback ask

Monica — thanks for the context, brief initial thoughts below. I ran a quick back-of-envelope using the attached traffic sheet and our per-node throughput for the two model classes.

Assumptions (quick):
- 13B avg tokens per request: 8, 70B avg tokens per request: 18
- Weighted model mix: 60% 13B, 40% 70B
- Effective per-node sustained concurrency (13B): ~12 ongoing inference sessions
- Effective per-node sustained concurrency (70B): ~5 ongoing inference sessions

Preliminary steady-state node recommendation (round numbers):
- US: 160 nodes (covers ~65% traffic with 25% headroom)
- EU: 60 nodes (covers ~23% traffic with 20% headroom)
- APAC: 30 nodes (covers ~12% traffic with 25% headroom)

Burst/headroom: I recommend a 25–30% burst buffer for Q1 onboarding if we can't provision instant capacity. We should reserve a small hot pool of +10% in US for the canary stage.

Fallback lanes:
- If APAC constrained: route APAC traffic to nearest EU nodes for non-low-latency customers; for critical routes, fall back to hosted (shared) with strict rate limits and prefetched KV cache per customer.
- Canary order: US -> EU -> APAC (US first to verify model parity and scaling behavior).

Open items I need from Helix: more granular country-level peak hour multipliers and a target failover latency cap for APAC users if we route to EU.

I'll follow up with a short spreadsheet mapping node counts to expected tail latency per model after we get the peak multipliers.

-rishi

Folks — attaching a brief cost delta and recommended commit structure (attachment: SOW-draft-helix.docx). Highlights below: 

Option A — Immediate provision (12-month term)
- US: 160 nodes, EU: 60 nodes, APAC: 30 nodes
- One-time provisioning premium: +18% on top of monthly run-rate for priority scheduling
- Estimated monthly committed cost: $242k

Option B — Tranche commit (3 tranches over 90 days)
- Initial commit: 120 US / 40 EU / 20 APAC (covers ~75% steady). Subsequent tranches provision on milestone delivery.
- Lower immediate cash outlay but +7% effective unit cost due to staging and coordination
- Estimated monthly committed cost (after full provisioning): $255k

Recommendation: Pursue Option B with a short-term burst buffer (hot pool) in US to support the canary; this mitigates cash and procurement friction while keeping latency targets.

Next steps: I'll upload the SOW-draft-helix.docx to the Drive and share a DocuSign link for signature-ready terms if Helix wants the immediate provision path.
